newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 11.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning.

News Corp Ltd chief executive and chairman Rupert Murdoch said in a newspaper interview published on Friday that News was still on track for a 20 percent increase in profit in the current 1996/97 year. Murdoch also told the Courier Mail newspaper that he did not want to buy John Fairfax Holdings Ltd. He also said he expected the government to remove the cross-media ownership rules and that Kerry Packer would get what he wanted from the government's inquiry into the rules. But he also said Packer did not want to buy Fairfax and had actually tried to sell his shares three times in the last 12 months.

A poker game over the future of Australian transport firm TNT Ltd has started between 19.99 percent shareholder Bankers Trust Australia (BTA) and takeover bidder Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV, analysts say. On Thursday the Federal Court on Thursday removed an order against two Australian firms which had been involved in trading in options of transport group TNT Ltd.

Memtec Ltd said overnight in the United States it plans to proceed with its proposed $280-million stock acquisition of Gelman Sciences Inc, despite the news that Gelman is in talks with Pall Corp about a possible deal. The ADSs of Memtec rose 3-5/8 to 30-5/8 on doubts about the deal, analysts said.

Newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it had experienced a flat first quarter and expected similar conditions for the rest of 1996/97. Chief financial officer and board member John Greaves said the slow economy and its impact on advertising volumes meant the full year would not be much better than the first three months. Asked how the first quarter went, Greaves told Reuters: "Pretty flat, not good." "We expected a pretty disinteresting first quarter and we saw the results. I mean ad volumes across the media sector as a whole had been pretty low," he said. Fairfax also said on Thursday it had mandated Westpac Banking Corp to arrange a A$400 million combined promissory note and medium-term note programme.

Several thousand staff of ANZ Banking Group (New Zealand) Ltd went on strike on Friday over a pay dispute, the Finsec trade union said. General Secretary Paul Goulter said the strike was expected to be for just one day except in Wellington, where workers voted to strike again on Monday.

Joe White Maltings Ltd said on Thursday that the latest takeover bid of an effective A$5.44 per share for the malster by Ridley Corp Ltd was neither fair nor reasonable and should be rejected by shareholders.
